checks.name: 48_samples_to_odd_columns
checks.detail: 48 tubes -> 48 wells, odd columns only: True

checks.name: step_order
checks.detail: expected per well: beads > isopropanol > sample > remove > ethanol > remove > ethanol > remove > elution > recover

checks.name: fresh_tip_per_sample_no_cross_contact
checks.detail: 48 distinct tips for 48 sample transfers; violations: []

checks.name: recover_about_80ul
checks.detail: 70-90 uL of the 100 uL eluate, as the task's step 13 says; 48/48 sample wells

items.evidence: apiLevel 2.11 with metadata; p300 multi only handles 40–200 µL aliquots, p1000 handles 250/540 µL; waste wells peak ~1540 µL (<2400); reservoir_columns_within_15ml passed.

Every tip is dropped; p1000 uses a fresh tip per sample and per removal; multi tips that touch sample wells are replaced per column; fresh_tip_per_sample_no_cross_contact passed with 48 distinct tips.
All 14 steps are in order with the right volumes and delays (5 min, 4 min, 4 min dry, 30 s, 90 s), 4 °C set before elution, 80 µL recovered, magnet disengaged at the end; all 18 checks passed.
sample_wells are the odd columns 1,3,5,7,9,11 of the mag plate and tubes come from slot 10 then slot 7; 48_samples_to_odd_columns and distinct_elution_wells passed.
Code adds 40 µL beads, then 150+100 µL isopropanol, then 250 µL sample with mix(5, 250); delay 5 min, engage, delay 4 min, then removes 540 µL with the magnet on.
Two loops add 500 µL ethanol (200+200+100) and remove it to waste with the magnet engaged, then delay(minutes=4) with the magnet on, then magdeck.disengage().
Magnet is disengaged, 100 µL elution buffer is added and mixed 10x, then delay 30 s, engage, delay 90 s, and aspirate(80) goes to a distinct elution well (recover_about_80ul passed).

judge.summary: The protocol simulates cleanly and passes all 18 run-log checks. It follows the 14 steps with the correct volumes, timings, magnet states and per-sample tips. I scored every rubric item 1, and the only doubt is the multichannel tip that dispenses ethanol into wells and is reused.
